# 2.2.2 Vector Scaling

**Definition 2.2.2.1** (Vector Scaling). \ Vector scaling is multipying each element $v_i$ of the vector $\mathbf{v} \in \mathbb{R}^n$ with a scalar  $\alpha \in \mathbb{R}$ to yeild another vector $\mathbf{w}$.
$$
\alpha \mathbf{v} = \alpha \begin{bmatrix} v_1\\ v_2\\ \vdots\\ v_n \end{bmatrix} = \begin{bmatrix} \alpha v_1\\ \alpha v_2\\ \vdots\\ \alpha v_n \end{bmatrix} \in \mathbb{R}^n
$$
Where,
$$
\mathbf{L} :  \mathbb{R} \times \mathbb{R}^n \rightarrow \mathbb{R}^n
$$
\
\

**Example 2.2.2.1**
$$
5 \begin{bmatrix} 4\\ 6\\ \end{bmatrix} = \begin{bmatrix} 5*4\\ 5*6\\ \end{bmatrix} = \begin{bmatrix} 20\\ 30\\ \end{bmatrix} \in \mathbb{R}^2
$$
